'''Anagrams''' in Star Wars CCG are character (and a few other) titles that scramble the names of Decipher staff, Lucasfilm contacts, squadron members, pets, and movie in-jokes. They have no effect on play. Hidden-image eggs are on [[Easter eggs]], and jokes in card text on [[Jokes]].<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 200. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref>

A fan page collected the list while Decipher employees were still adding them; two unnamed Decipher people confirmed Premiere still hid names and that the public list was incomplete.<ref name="geo">[https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at oocities.org (GeoCities mirror). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008200413/https://www.oocities.org/collegepark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Internet Archive], 8 October 2026.</ref><ref name="geo2">[https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at geocities.ws. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261012174750/https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/anagrams.html Internet Archive], 12 October 2026.</ref><ref name="reo">[https://web.archive.org/web/20160406045459/http://www.reocities.com/CollegePark/plaza/9433/anagrams.html Anagramed Decipherians] at reocities.com (archive, 6 April 2016)</ref>

Some titles scramble only part of a name. [[Nabrun Leids]] scrambles Braunlich, the surname of [[Tom Braunlich]]; [[Lieutenant Tarn Mison]] scrambles Martinson; and [[Imperial Trooper Guard Dainsom]] scrambles Madison.<ref name="encyc" /> The [[Theed Palace]] card [[Dams Denna]] (2001) is an exact anagram of [[Dan Madsen]], president of the Official Star Wars Fan Club, who appears in its picture as the kaadu handler from ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="wook-damsdenna" />

The card picture is "Alien 23", an alien maquette made for ''Return of the Jedi'' but never used in the film, which the crew called "the thinker among aliens".<ref name="swcom">Kevin Beentjes, [https://www.starwars.com/news/back-from-the-drawing-board-recycled-star-wars-aliens Back from the Drawing Board: Recycled Star Wars Aliens], StarWars.com (October 2014). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20141007212642/http://www.starwars.com/news/back-from-the-drawing-board-recycled-star-wars-aliens Internet Archive], 7 October 2014.</ref>

| [[Niado Duegad]]
| [[File:SE-D-niadoduegad.gif|180px|link=Niado Duegad|alt=Niado Duegad original card]]
| Dianoga Dude
| [[File:Anagram reference - Dianoga in the Death Star trash compactor in Star Wars.jpg|x250px|alt=The dianoga's eyestalk rising out of the garbage in the Death Star trash compactor]]
| Decipher's photo for this card shows "Alien 18", an alien model built for ''Return of the Jedi'' that looks like a [[Dianoga|dianoga]]. It was dropped from the film because it was too hard to operate.<ref name="swcom" /> With no name from the film to use, Decipher called him a "Dianoga Dude" and scrambled the letters into ''Niado Duegad'', which uses exactly the same eleven letters. Dianogas are tentacled carnivores that live in stagnant water and garbage and drag their prey under, so usually only the eyestalk shows. The best-known one lives in the Death Star trash compactor in ''Star Wars'' (1977).<ref name="sw-dianoga">[https://www.starwars.com/databank/dianoga Dianoga], StarWars.com Databank. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261014053301/https://www.starwars.com/databank/dianoga Internet Archive], 14 October 2026.</ref> The card's lore gives Niado an unrelated backstory, as a mercenary from Vodran, and doesn't mention dianogas. The 1990s fan list "Anagramed Decipherians" spells the answer "Diaogana Dude". That spelling has one more A than the card has, so it is most likely a typo.<ref name="geo" />

| Game designer. [[Jerry Darcy]] was Decipher's lead SWCCG designer from ''A New Hope'' (1996) through ''Endor'' (1999).<ref name="holo-lead" /> ''Rayc Ryjerd'' uses exactly the letters of Jerry Darcy.<ref name="geo" />

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261027184736/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenner_Products Internet Archive], 27 October 2026.</ref>

Marketing Dept., Product Champion Coordinator".
